arxiv-1809-10531.creator: Sang Won Bae, Michiel Smid
arxiv-1809-10531.description: Abstract In the range closest pair problem, we want to construct a data structure storing a set S S of n n points in the plane, such that for any axes-parallel query rectangle R R , the closest pair in the set R ∩ S R\cap S can be reported.

arxiv-2101-05973.title: Anisotropic chiral cosmology: exact solutions
arxiv-2101-05973.creator: Luis Rey Díaz-Barrón, Abraham Espinoza-García, S. Pérez-Payán, J. Socorro
arxiv-2101-05973.description: Abstract In this work, we investigate the anisotropic Bianchi type I cosmological model in the chiral setup, in a twofold manner. Firstly, we consider a quintessence plus a k-essence like model, where two scalar fields but only one potential term is considered.

arxiv-2111-05505.title: DACFL: Dynamic Average Consensus Based Federated Learning in Decentralized Topology Thanks: Zhikun Chen and Daofeng Li are with the Department of Electronic Engineering and Information Science, School of Information Science and Technology, University of Science and Technology of China. Address: No.
arxiv-2111-05505.creator: Zhikun Chen, Daofeng Li, Jinkang Zhu, Sihai Zhang
arxiv-2111-05505.description: Abstract Federated learning (FL) is a burgeoning distributed machine learning framework where a central parameter server (PS) coordinates many local users to train a globally consistent model. Conventional federated learning inevitably relies on a centralized topology with a PS. As a result, it will paralyze once the PS fails.

arxiv-2202-03045.title: Metric-valued regression
arxiv-2202-03045.creator: Dan Tsir Cohen, Aryeh Kontorovich
arxiv-2202-03045.description: Abstract We propose an efficient algorithm for learning mappings between two metric spaces, 𝒳 {\cal X} and 𝒴 {\cal Y} . Our procedure is strongly Bayes-consistent whenever 𝒳 {\cal X} and 𝒴 {\cal Y} are topologically separable and 𝒴 {\cal Y} is “bounded in expectation” (our term; the separability assumption can be somewhat weakened).

arxiv-2206-13826.title: Suppressed fluctuations as the origin of the static magnetic order in strained Sr 2 RuO 4
arxiv-2206-13826.creator: Bongjae Kim 1, Sergii Khmelevskyi 2, Cesare Franchini 3,4, I. I. Mazin 5,6
arxiv-2206-13826.description: Abstract Combining first principle density functional calculations and Moriya’s self-consistent renormalization theory, we explain the recently reported counterintuitive appearance of an ordered magnetic state in uniaxially strained Sr 2 RuO 4 beyond the Lifshits transition. We show that strain weakens the quantum spin ﬂuctuations, which destroy the static order, more strongly than the tendency to magnetism.

arxiv-2209-11742.title: A Frequency-Agile Image-Reject Channelizer for Spaceborne 0–50 MHz Radio Spectroscopy
arxiv-2209-11742.creator: Hassan ElSayed
arxiv-2209-11742.description: Abstract Spaceborne low-frequency radio instruments open spectral windows that are inaccessible or strongly compromised from the ground and are used for measurements ranging from solar radio bursts and plasma waves to the low-frequency Galactic background. We investigate a frequency-agile analog receiver intended as the channelization stage of a compact spaceborne radio spectrometer.

arxiv-2306-14628.title: An Integral Projection-based Semantic Autoencoder for Zero-Shot Learning
arxiv-2306-14628.creator: William Heyden, Habib Ullah, M. Salman Siddiqui, Fadi Al Machot
arxiv-2306-14628.description: Abstract Zero-shot Learning (ZSL) classification categorizes or predicts classes (labels) that are not included in the training set (unseen classes). Recent works proposed different semantic autoencoder (SAE) models where the encoder embeds a visual feature vector space into the semantic space and the decoder reconstructs the original visual feature space.

arxiv-2309-10511.title: Self2Seg: Single-Image Self-Supervised Joint Segmentation and Denoising
arxiv-2309-10511.creator: Nadja Gruber J. Schwab N. Debroux N. Papadakis M. Haltmeier
arxiv-2309-10511.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Nadja Gruber J. Schwab N. Debroux N. Papadakis M. Haltmeier. We develop Self2Seg, a self-supervised method for the joint segmentation and denoising of a single image. To this end, we combine the advantages of variational segmentation with self-supervised deep learning. One major benefit of our method lies in the fact, that in contrast to data-driven methods, where huge amounts of labeled samples are necessary, Self2Seg segments an image into meaningful regions without any training database.

arxiv-2311-04360.title: Normal form of bimeromorphically contractible
arxiv-2311-04360.creator: holomorphic Lagrangian submanifolds
arxiv-2311-04360.description: Abstract Abstract Let M be a holomorphically symplectic complex manifold, not necessarily compact or quasiprojective, and X\subset M a compact Lagrangian submanifold. We construct a deformation to the normal cone, showing that a neighbourhood of X can be deformed to its neighbourhood in T^{*}X . This is used to study Lagrangian submanifolds which can be bimeromorphically contracted to a point.

arxiv-2405-07642.title: Tidal disruption event AT2020ocn: early–time X–ray flares caused by a possible disc alignment process
arxiv-2405-07642.creator: Z. Cao, P.G. Jonker, D.R. Pasham, S. Wen, N.C. Stone, A.I. Zabludoff
arxiv-2405-07642.description: Abstract A tidal disruption event (TDE) may occur when a star is torn apart by the tidal force of a black hole (BH). Eventually, an accretion disc is thought to form out of stellar debris falling back towards the BH.

arxiv-2411-14649.title: Coupled electron-phonon hydrodynamics in two-dimensional semiconductors
arxiv-2411-14649.creator: Yujie Quan, Bolin Liao
arxiv-2411-14649.description: Abstract Electronic and thermal transport properties in two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors have been extensively investigated due to their potential to miniaturize transistors. Microscopically, electron-phonon interactions are considered the dominant momentum relaxation mechanism for electrons that limits carrier mobility beyond cryogenic temperatures.

arxiv-2504-01550.title: Representation Bending for Large Language Model Safety
arxiv-2504-01550.creator: Ashkan Yousefpour, Taeheon Kim, Ryan S. Kwon, Seungbeen Lee, Wonje Jeung, Seungju Han, Alvin Wan, Harrison Ngan, Youngjae Yu, Jonghyun Choi, Seoul National University, Yonsei University, AIM Intelligence, University of Michigan, Stanford University, Amazon AWS
arxiv-2504-01550.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have emerged as powerful tools, but their inherent safety risks – ranging from harmful content generation to broader societal harms – pose significant challenges. These risks can be amplified by the recent adversarial attacks, fine-tuning vulnerabilities, and the increasing deployment of LLMs in high-stakes environments.

arxiv-2506-02049.title: EvoGit: Decentralized Code Evolution via Git-Based Multi-Agent Collaboration
arxiv-2506-02049.creator: Beichen Huang, Ran Cheng, Kay Chen Tan
arxiv-2506-02049.description: Abstract We introduce EvoGit, a decentralized multi-agent framework for collaborative software development driven by autonomous code evolution. EvoGit deploys a population of independent coding agents, each proposing edits to a shared codebase without centralized coordination, explicit message passing, or shared memory.

arxiv-2507-04749.title: MatDecompSDF: High-Fidelity 3D Shape and PBR Material Decomposition from Multi-View Images
arxiv-2507-04749.creator: Chengyu Wang, Isabella Bennett, Henry Scott, Liang Zhang, Mei Chen, Hao Li, Rui Zhao
arxiv-2507-04749.description: Abstract . We present MatDecompSDF, a novel framework for recovering high-fidelity 3D shapes and decomposing their physically-based material properties from multi-view images. The core challenge of inverse rendering lies in the ill-posed disentanglement of geometry, materials, and illumination from 2D observations.

arxiv-2508-04306.title: Multi-Agent Taskforce Collaboration: Self-Correction of Compounding Errors in Long-Form Literature Review Generation
arxiv-2508-04306.creator: Zhi Zhang, Yan Liu, Zhejing Hu, Gong Chen, Sheng-hua Zhong, Jiannong Cao
arxiv-2508-04306.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Zhi Zhang, Yan Liu, Zhejing Hu, Gong Chen, Sheng-hua Zhong, Jiannong Cao. Literature reviews play an important role in scientific research. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have boosted the development of automated systems for the entire literature review workflow, from retrieval to manuscript drafting. However, a key challenge is that mistakes made in early stages can propagate and amplify in subsequent steps, leading to compounding errors that undermine the faithfulness of the final review.

arxiv-2510-03656.title: Wormholes in Einstein-Dirac-Maxwell theory with identical spacetime asymptotics
arxiv-2510-03656.creator: Vladimir Dzhunushaliev, Vladimir Folomeev, Nurzada Beissen, Adilet Nurmukhamedov
arxiv-2510-03656.description: Abstract Within general relativity, we study spherically symmetric configurations with wormhole topology consisting of spinor fields and a Maxwell electric field. For such a system, we construct complete families of regular asymmetric solutions describing wormholes connecting two identical Minkowski spacetimes.

pmc-10644253.title: Fusing the spatial structure of electroencephalogram channels can increase the individualization of the functional connectivity network
pmc-10644253.creator: Ming Li, Jun Yang, Wenli Tian, Xiangyu Ju
pmc-10644253.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). An electroencephalogram (EEG) functional connectivity (FC) network is individualized and plays a significant role in EEG-based person identification. Traditional FC networks are constructed by statistical dependence and correlation between EEG channels, without considering the spatial relationships between the channels. The individual identification algorithm based on traditional FC networks is sensitive to the integrity of channels and crucially relies on signal preprocessing; therefore, finding a new presentation for FC networks may help increase the performance of the identification algorithms.

pmc-11333802.title: Long-Term Outcomes of Gamma Knife Radiosurgery for Cerebral Cavernous Malformations: 10 Years and Beyond
pmc-11333802.creator: Ho Sung Myeong, Sang Soon Jeong, Jung Hoon Kim, Jae Meen Lee, Kwang Hyon Park, Kawngwoo Park, Hyun Joo Park, Hye Ran Park, Byung Woo Yoon, Eun Jung Lee, Jin Wook Kim, Hyun Tai Chung, Dong Gyu Kim, Sun Ha Paek
pmc-11333802.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundWe aimed to evaluate long-term outcomes of gamma knife radiosurgery (GKS) for cerebral cavernous malformations (CCMs).MethodsAmong the 233 CCM patients who underwent GKS, 79 adult patients (96 lesions) followed for over 10 years were included and analyzed retrospectively. Annual hemorrhage rate (AHR) was analyzed the entire cohort of 233 patients and the subset of 79 enrolled patients by dividing lesions into overall CCM lesions and brainstem lesions.

pmc-11464542.title: Seasonal and diel patterns in Black Sea harbour porpoise acoustic activity in 2020–2022
pmc-11464542.creator: Julia Ivanchikova, Nick Tregenza, Dimitar Popov, Galina Meshkova, Romulus‐Marian Paiu, Costin Timofte, Ayaka Amaha Öztürk, Arda M Tonay, Ayhan Dede, Uğur Özsandıkçı, Natia Kopaliani, Davit Dekanoidze, Zurab Gurielidze, Karina Vishnyakova, Philip S Hammond, Pavel Gol'din
pmc-11464542.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The Black Sea is a semi‐enclosed inland sea with an unevenly distributed extensive coastal shelf area and anoxic deep waters. It is inhabited by common and bottlenose dolphins, as well as harbour porpoises, all represented by local subspecies. Between September 2020 and October 2022, 19 F‐PODs deployed by research teams from Bulgaria, Georgia, Romania, Türkiye and Ukraine collected data on acoustic activity of Black Sea harbour porpoises. Strong seasonal and diel patterns were found, which varied in three regions.

pmc-12436559.description: The increase in glycerol availability as a byproduct of biodiesel production has attracted attention in its utilization as a carbon source for microbial fermentation. pmc-12610131.title: Real-Time Defect Identification in Automotive Brake Calipers Using PCA-Optimized Feature Extraction and Machine Learning
pmc-12610131.creator: Juwon Lee, Ukyong Woo, Myung-Hun Lee, Jin-Young Kim, Hajin Choi, Taekeun Oh
pmc-12610131.description: This study aims to develop a non-contact automated impact-acoustic measurement system (AIAMS) for real-time detection of manufacturing defects in automotive brake calipers, a key component of the Electric Parking Brake (EPB) system. Calipers hold brake pads in contact with discs, and defects caused by repeated loads and friction can lead to reduced braking performance and abnormal vibration and noise.

pmc-13621457.title: Balancing gain and diversity: Optimal contribution selection for sustainable genetic improvement in sugarcane
pmc-13621457.creator: Natalya Vo Van‐Zivkovic, Ben J Hayes, Karen Aitken, Eric Dinglasan, Terry Morgan, Seema Yadav
pmc-13621457.description: Sugarcane (Saccharum spp. hybrids), the source of ∼80% of the worlds sugar, has experienced a plateau in genetic improvement over recent decades. This stagnation is largely due to the crop's complex polyploid genome and long breeding cycles, which limit the efficiency of traditional selection methods.
